overall: The AG found no Open Meeting Law violation: the Board reasonably believed an officer's harassment report was laying groundwork for litigation, so its Sept. 24 executive session under Purpose 3 was proper.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Board discussed an officer's mental health and discipline in executive session on Sept. 24 without giving him the individual notice required under Purpose 1.
allegations.key_passage: we find that the Board did not violate the Open Meeting Law when it met in executive session under Purpose 3 on September 24.

allegations.summary: Complainant argued that where a discussion fits both Purpose 1 and Purpose 3, the body must comply with the requirements of both purposes.
allegations.key_passage: When a discussion may properly be held under multiple executive session purposes, the public body may choose which executive session purpose(s) to cite.

allegations.summary: Complainant argued no discrimination or retaliation claims were threatened or imminent, so the Board could not justify executive session under Purpose 3 (litigation strategy).
allegations.key_passage: Considering the totality of the circumstances, we find that the Board properly met in executive session under Purpose 3 to discuss strategy with respect to litigation the Board reasonably believed was clearly and imminently threatened.
